proposed_comments.title: Preserve and revalidate the package captured trust state
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve and revalidate the package captured trust state

**Severity:** `critical`

The final package check compares only the captured package identity, and it skips the metadata policy whenever the original approval was for an unverified package. That means the same package identity can still be accepted after it becomes modified, stubbed, unavailable, external, mutable, or changes content-integrity state between the warning and activation.

Capture the deployment and integrity fields with the initial `PackageIdentity`, repeat integrity verification during `IsCurrent` when it was part of the captured state, and reject any state transition before activation.

**Verification:** Add focused regressions showing that an unchanged approved-unverified package remains eligible, while modified, stubbed, unavailable, external, mutable, and changed-integrity registrations fail revalidation.

confidence.rationale: Current-head PackageIdentity stores only identity/signing metadata, while PackageVerification::details::IsCurrent skips MetadataEligible for approved-unverified targets and therefore does not compare modified, stub, status, external/mutable, or integrity-state transitions.

proposed_comments.title: Fail closed for filesystem targets that are not fully protected
proposed_comments.body:
### Fail closed for filesystem targets that are not fully protected

**Severity:** `critical`

`SignatureVerification::IsCurrent` delegates non-package targets to package revalidation, and that path returns current whenever `target.package` is empty. As a result, absolute non-`.exe` paths, relative paths, drive-relative paths such as `C:app.exe`, and verified executables whose writable parent directories can be renamed after approval can pass the final check without protecting the filesystem namespace that `ShellExecuteEx` resolves.

Distinguish URI/protocol targets from filesystem targets, reject every filesystem target that lacks a retained executable handle, and keep non-delete-sharing handles for each parent directory through the elevation request. If any required directory cannot be protected, fail the verification instead of allowing approval to proceed.

**Verification:** Add regressions for absolute `.exe`, `.lnk` or script, ordinary relative and drive-relative paths, plus a URI case confirming legitimate protocol targets remain supported.

confidence.rationale: Current-head SignatureVerification::IsCurrent delegates every target to PackageVerification::IsCurrent; non-package targets return true when target.package is empty, regardless of whether a file handle exists or directory namespace protection was retained.
